title: Lenny's "Grand Unifying Theory of Growth": four steps from first users to growth engines
summary: Lenny brainstorms a zero-to-scale growth playbook: pick a wedge early adopter, craft a remarkable value prop, find them through concentric circles of channels, then commit to one of four growth engines. He backs it with many company examples and open discussion on the messy middle and on humane growth.

principles.text: Start with a narrow early-adopter wedge into a bigger market, then a value prop that resonates with them.
principles.quote: step one is identify your early adopter users who are kind of a wedge into a broader market step two is identify a value prop that resonates with these specific users

principles.text: Aim for a value prop that is genuinely remarkable, so people want to talk about it.
principles.quote: remarkable just means it's worth remarking about and so what you want to figure out is a value prop that is remarkable to the people you're pitching to

principles.text: Early users come from concentric circles around the founder; friends and colleagues bootstrap trust, especially in B2B.
principles.quote: it's more that if there's a reason to believe that it's worth trying so just bootstrapping trust

principles.text: Early tactics spike but don't last; you need a sustainable growth engine, and there are only four: paid, virality, content/SEO, sales.
principles.quote: everything that we've talked about so far is not sustainable and it's not going to last it's going to be like a spike of growth

principles.text: Be the best in the world at one engine in your market; competitors then win through other engines.
principles.quote: you need to be the best in the world at one of these engines in your market

principles.text: Once you know which engine will drive growth, commit to it instead of poking at it on the side.
principles.quote: if you know that's where you're gonna drive growth from you should just commit to it and and focus on and move as fast as you can
